title: hybrid-cudagraph-fallback-and-dynamic-kernel-selection-for-fragmented-batches
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: we observed sporadic cudagraph replay regressions when request batch shapes are highly fragmented (short prefix tokens followed by long continuations) and when op-level kernel selection switches between fast-path and fallback implementations. This PR introduces a hybrid capture strategy that records a compact shape-invariant fingerprint, uses a lighter-weight runtime validator at replay time, and integrates a dynamic kernel selector to prefer capture-stable kernels during warmup. The change reduces replay failure rates and avoids conservative shape guards that previously prevented reuse. Approach summary: 1) Add a CaptureFingerprint produced during initial capture that summarizes sequence-length histogram, KV cache usage flags, and quantization mode so that replay can quickly decide compatibility without exact-shape guards. 2) Implement a HybridFallbackManager that tries the captured graph, runs a micro-warmup (<=8 tokens) using the new validator, and falls back to per-step execution only on mismatch. 3) Extend KernelSelector to expose a "capture-stability" metric; the scheduler prefers kernels marked stable when running in cudagraph-enabled routes or during canary warmups. 4) Add telemetry (cudagraph.replay.{attempts,successes,validated_fallbacks}, kernel.selector.choice) and a feature flag runtime.cudagraph.hybrid_fallback to allow staged rollout. Performance/regression results: canary run across 20 instances with synthetic shard workloads shows 6-12% throughput improvement for long-seq workloads versus current main while reducing replay failure rate from ~7% to 0.3% on fragmented traffic. Median latency p50/p95 unchanged within noise; p99 improved slightly for batched workloads due to fewer fallback hot paths. Compatibility notes: this does not change model formats. The hybrid fingerprint is backward-compatible; nodes without the new runtime will ignore the fingerprint. We ship the feature behind the runtime flag and add a 2-week progressive rollout. Migration checklist: - Enable runtime.cudagraph.hybrid_fallback on staging; - Run perf benchmark-lab suite (bench/cudagraph) under both contiguous and fragmented batch profiles; - Monitor new metrics in console and SLO alerts. Related: ENG-1423 kernel-selection tuning, ENG-1458 canary rollout plan. Testing: unit tests for fingerprint equality and validator, integration perf tests, and end-to-end canary with real traffic. See docs/ops/cudagraphs.md for operator rollout steps and a short note in CHANGELOG about the flag.

review_comments: Marco Liu: The fingerprint looks promising but we should ensure it does not add CPU overhead on hot paths. Can the serializer be caching-friendly?
Asha Patel: The serializer uses a fixed-size bitmap and a preallocated buffer; microbenchmarks show <0.5% CPU overhead on capture path in our perf lab.
Priya Rao: We need clearer guidance in docs about when to disable hybrid_fallback for low-memory devices.
Asha Patel: Added section in docs/ops/cudagraphs.md about memory tradeoffs and a knob runtime.cudagraph.max_warmup_tokens (default 8).
Daniel Kim: Can we add a quick telemetry-based alert to detect increased validated_fallbacks?
Asha Patel: Added cudagraph.replay.validated_fallbacks to console dashboard and a leak-style alert rule in ci/canary/manifest.yaml.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash on 2025-12-03 after required approvals and successful canary run.
release_notes: Feature: hybrid cudagraph fallback and dynamic kernel selection to improve replay robustness on fragmented batch shapes. Improvements: lower replay failure rate, modest throughput gains for long sequences. Ops: new runtime flag runtime.cudagraph.hybrid_fallback (default off), new metric cudagraph.replay.validated_fallbacks, rollout steps in docs/ops/cudagraphs.md.
